summary: Whatcom County, WA: camp from 1929, L-4 cab on the summit in 1932; abandoned 1968, cabin burned 1973; remnants of a phone pole and tramway; public status unstated.

facts.design: L-4 cabs: the first on the primary summit in 1932, a second on a minor summit a mile east
facts.status_note: The cabin burned in 1973; photo captions describe a phone pole and tramway remnants

visit.trail_note: About 7 miles one way with about 6,400 feet of gain, per WillhiteWeb; the route is mostly easy but exposed class 3 scrambling, with perhaps one low class 4 move

events.note: Camp established; George Hadley named as the first watcher
L-4 cab built on the primary summit
Gary Snyder; HistoryLink says he spent six weeks on the mountain
Tommy Buller nailed the old cab shut and moved the firefinder to a newer L-4 cab on a lower summit a mile east; FFLOS dates the new cab to about 1950

resolved_conflicts.explanation: FFLOS dates the newer east cab to about 1950; firelookout and WillhiteWeb date it to 1955. The record uses 1955, which two sources agree on, and the story flags the disagreement.

FFLOS registers the site at 7,761 feet; firelookout gives 8128 and 7054 feet and WillhiteWeb gives 8,128 feet. The register figure is kept as the record's elevation, and the story notes the difference.

notes_for_editor: firelookout.com and FFLOS share much wording, so they are not fully independent. The 1950 vs 1955 date is unresolved. No access level is recorded because no source states whether the summit is open to the public. A trailgroove.com search snippet (not read) calls Snyder the last occupant in 1952, which conflicts with the 1955 date; not verified and not used. A whatcomtalk.com 2024 article did not name Crater Mountain in the text read, so its volcano-monitoring reference is not used. Brief status 'gone' is correct.
